description:
petroleum/crude_distillation.rs, part 1. A BlackOilCrude spec (API gravity, gas specific gravity, GOR, BS&W) that produces a pseudo-component slate.

The composition is exact rather than approximate: black_oil::oil_specific_gravity_from_api, ::liquid_molecular_weight and ::liquid_normal_boiling_point produce precisely the three Option fields BulkAssay carries (specific_gravity_60f, molar_mass, average_boiling_point), which BulkCharacterizationOptions then hands to generate_compounds.

Acceptance: a named reference crude (pick a real published API/SG, cite it) yields a monotonic pseudo-component slate — boiling points ascending, mole fractions summing to 1, every Tc/Pc/omega finite and physical. Assert against the black-oil correlations' own published ranges, and state where the crude sits relative to them.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Done. BlackOilCrude -> BulkAssay -> pseudo-component slate works and is tested (5 tests).

The composition turned out to be exact rather than approximate: black_oil::oil_specific_gravity_from_api, ::liquid_molecular_weight and ::liquid_normal_boiling_point produce precisely the three Option fields BulkAssay carries. Viscosity fields are deliberately left None so generate_compounds falls back to Abbott's correlation rather than being handed a fabricated measurement.

Measured for the 38 degAPI light-sweet reference crude: SG 0.8348, MW 206.5 g/mol, mean NBP 538.8 K. An 8-cut slate spans normal boiling points 390.1 K to 825.2 K with mole fractions summing to 1 within 1e-9 and all Tc/Pc/omega finite and monotonic.

Tests assert: API<->SG round-trip is inverse to <1e-12; all three bulk properties land in crude-like ranges; a heavier crude (22 degAPI) characterises as heavier on all three; the slate normalises; CrudeCut bands tile the temperature axis with no gaps.

ONE THING THE SLATE REVEALED that matters downstream: the heaviest cut has an acentric factor of 1.16, far past the omega < 0.49 limit of standard Peng-Robinson's kappa correlation. That is a property of a real crude's heavy end, not a bug here, but it means PR cannot be used on this slate — see op-190j.2.

title: crude: black-oil -> BulkAssay -> pseudo-component slate

description: Make TampinesSteamArray an all-Mach hybrid: keep the pressure-based PIMPLE skeleton, inject KNP central-upwind (rhoCentralFoam) dissipation as a Mach-weighted beta(Ma) deferred-correction flux. Copy the KNP flux MATH into tampines (NO outram-foam dependency; tampines already has all types + speed of sound w_ph_wood_wallis; preserve GPLv3/OpenFOAM provenance header). Opt-in SolverMode{Pimple,HybridAllMach}, default Pimple => beta=0 => bit-identical to current => plateau fix + 915 tests preserved by construction. Goal: damp the near-sonic ringing at the Edwards flashing front while retaining the plateau/no-subcooling.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
notes.content: MAINTAINER DIRECTIVE (2026-07-16): TampinesSteamArray must be HEM through-and-through — the equilibrium sound speed (Kieffer, above), the KNP wave speeds (u +/- a_HEM), and critical/choked flow all use the HEM equilibrium closure. Critical flow is already HEM (the break BC uses get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_multiphase_ph, the validated HEM choked-flow dispatcher). No Wood-Wallis, no frozen, no perfect-gas anywhere.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
notes.content: Core deliverable DONE (B1-B6 closed). SolverMode{Pimple(default),HybridAllMach} opt-in; default Pimple bit-identical (915 baseline + 5 new central_upwind tests = 920 lib pass, 0 fail). HEM equilibrium sound speed throughout (Kieffer eq.28 in dome via s from (p,h) flash; w_tp_1/2/3/5 single-phase; NOT Wood-Wallis). KNP dissipation on continuity+momentum (energy carried implicitly by continuity-into-phi to preserve plateau cancellation); min(Ma) gating (low-Mach scaling avoids liquid-interface blowup); validity-edge guard. Edwards: ringing -55.5% (excess-TV 4670->2079), plateau retained 392.7->387.7 psia. Remaining: op-21g.15.7 (late-time >0.18s hardening). NOTE incident op-6zi (accidental revert destroyed uncommitted op-21g.14 ddt_coeff_old + set_outlet_velocity; reconstructed & verified via exact Pimple-full reproduction).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop
notes.content: MAINTAINER DECISION (2026-07-16): default SolverMode::Pimple (HEM-closed PIMPLE) is the VALIDATED, kept path — recovers the Edwards plateau (392.7 psia) and is stable over the full 600 ms. SolverMode::HybridAllMach is EXPERIMENTAL / future work: it damps the near-sonic ringing (~55%) over 0-0.15s but CRASHES past t~0.18s. Marked experimental in the SolverMode doc. The late-time instability (op-21g.15.7) is a substantial standalone work item, not a quick harden.

title: Hybrid all-Mach (rhoCentralFoam + rhoPimpleFoam) TampinesSteamArray

design:
Programme epic for the steady-state nuclear refinery on `outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs`.

**Do not implement the refinery in one pass.** This epic exists to hold the
hierarchy; work happens in the child epics, gated by the audit.

## Architectural rule (binding)

```
outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs      <- owns process physics
        ^
        |
outram-foam-appbuilder-lib       <- adapts process models to spatial FVM
        |
        v
outram-foam-basic-lib / FVM
```

`dwsim-libs` owns: material and energy streams, thermodynamics, chemical
thermodynamics, reaction networks/kinetics, steady-state unit operations,
flash/separation, flowsheet graph, recycle/tear solving, crude
characterization, conservative lumping, steady-state refinery simulation.

**DWSIM must not depend on Outram-FOAM.** Outram-FOAM owns conservation-equation
discretization and transient/spatial solution, and consumes DWSIM thermo/kinetic
closures rather than owning refinery chemistry.

**Prefer extending good existing Rust abstractions over reproducing DWSIM's
class hierarchy.**

## Audit performed while filing (2026-09-05) — read this before scoping anything

`crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs` v0.0.3, **682 `#[test]` markers, no
prelude, 1 example**. Top-level modules: clean_energies, columns, compressor,
cooler, dynamics, flowsheet, flowsheet_solver, expander, heat_exchanger,
heater, interpolation, mixer, petroleum, pipe, pump, reactions, reactors,
separator, splitter, thermo, valve.

**Far more is already ported than the programme text assumes.** Three findings
that should redirect effort:

### 1. LHHW catalytic kinetics already exist

`src/reactions.rs` already provides `langmuir_hinshelwood_rate`,
`with_langmuir_hinshelwood`, `adsorption_constant`, `denominator_value`,
`forward_rate_constant`, `reverse_rate_constant`, `equilibrium_constant`,
`with_reaction_heat`, `with_conversion`, plus `ReactionKind`, `ReactionBasis`
and `EquilibriumConstant`.

The programme asks for "a reusable LHHW catalytic kinetic framework rather than
refinery-unit-specific equations". **It exists.** Hydrotreating therefore needs
a *reaction network* and a packed-bed application of existing machinery, not new
kinetics infrastructure.

### 2. Reactors already exist

`src/reactors/`: `Pfr`, `Cstr`, `ConversionReactor`, `EquilibriumReactor`,
`GibbsReactor`, with `ReactorFeed`, `ReactorOutcome`, `ReactorModel`.

### 3. Thermodynamics and assay characterization are extensive

`src/thermo/` (35 files): cubic_eos, pr1978, prsv2_full, pr_lee_kesler, lkp,
chao_seader_grayson, activity, unifac / unifac_dortmund / unifac_lle,
**electrolyte, electrolyte_svle, sour_water, seawater**, stability, transport,
gibbs, gibbs_multiphase, and flashes: flash, flash_vlle, flash_lle, flash_sle,
flash_svlle, flash_insideout, flash_insideout_3p, flash_immiscible,
flash_single_comp, energy_flash.

VLE/VLLE/SLE/SVLLE are present. **Electrolyte and sour-water packages exist**,
which bear directly on desalter brine, acid-gas removal and wastewater.

`src/petroleum/` (16 files): `Assay`, `BulkAssay`, `CurveAssay`,
`AssayCurvePoint`, `DistillationCurveKind`, `PseudoComponent`, curve
conversion, Riazi correlations, TBP curve fitting, quality checks, and
correlation sets for critical T/P, acentric factor and molecular weight.

**The assay infrastructure the programme asks for largely exists** — the open
question is coverage and dogfoodability, not existence.

## What this means for sequencing

The audit (child epic 1) is not a formality. On this evidence the likely
shape of the real work is:

- **exposure and orchestration**, not porting — the recurring finding across
  three prior programmes (#58, #63, #70) has been *data model exists, access
  seam missing*, and this crate has no prelude at all
- **conservative lumping** (child epic 2) is genuinely new and is the main
  architectural gap
- **refinery unit models** (desalter, VDU, hydrotreater, FCC, SRU, TGTU) are
  genuinely missing
- reaction *networks* and *chemistry data* are missing; reaction *machinery*
  is not

## Fidelity language (binding on every child issue)

Every issue must state which level it targets:

- **Crude estimate** — conceptual flowsheets, conservation testing, rough
  heat/mass balances, API dogfooding. Black-oil/bulk crude, assumed
  efficiencies, coarse pseudocomponents, simplified CDU/VDU.
- **Engineering model** — measured assay, TBP/D1160, density/MW/viscosity
  characterization, sulfur/SARA where relevant, validated thermodynamics,
  conservative lumping, realistic CDU/VDU auxiliaries, validated reactions.
- **Predictive model** — refinery/crude-specific assay, operating data,
  calibrated unit models, validated yields/properties, detailed chemistry.

**Do not label the refinery predictive.** Convergence is not accuracy.

## Global conservation (binding)

The flowsheet must provide a global conservation report: total mass, C, H, S,
N, O, water, energy, and metals where represented.

- non-reacting unit -> **species** conserved
- reacting unit -> **elements** conserved
- representation change -> mass and elements conserved

```
C in crude + imported carbon
  = C in products + coke + captured CO2 + stack + flare + wastewater/sludge

S in crude
  = S in products + elemental S + stack/tail gas + flare + wastewater/sludge
```

**Make conservation failure loud.**

## Branch

`develop` only. **Do not merge or push to `main` as part of this programme.**

## Child epics

Filed separately, linked from this issue, with dependencies set in `bn`.
title: Nuclear refinery steady-state process platform
